Burkitt lymphoma: 3

A Burkitt lymphoma specimen shows juxtaposition of MYC with an immunoglobulin heavy-chain regulatory region. Which classic chromosomal rearrangement accounts for this molecular event and the resulting deregulated proliferative signaling in the tumor?

  1. Tingible-body macrophages among proliferating tumor cells
  2. Tumor lysis syndrome
  3. t(8;14) involving MYC and the immunoglobulin heavy-chain locus
  4. Burkitt lymphoma
  5. MYC activation
Answer and explanation

t(8;14) involving MYC and the immunoglobulin heavy-chain locus

This is the classic translocation; variant immunoglobulin-locus translocations also occur.

Option explanations

t(8;14) involving MYC and the immunoglobulin heavy-chain locus: This is the classic translocation; variant immunoglobulin-locus translocations also occur.

Burkitt lymphoma: A rapidly growing mature B-cell lymphoma with MYC rearrangement and a very high proliferative rate fits Burkitt lymphoma. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

MYC activation: Dysregulated MYC promotes the rapid proliferation characteristic of Burkitt lymphoma. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Tingible-body macrophages among proliferating tumor cells: Macrophages containing apoptotic debris create the pale stars in the starry-sky pattern. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Tumor lysis syndrome: Rapid cell breakdown can produce hyperkalemia, hyperphosphatemia, hyperuricemia and kidney injury before or after therapy. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
